prompt.text: Which shape best describes the DOM?

hints: Parents hold children, and a child may hold more.
cards.fullLine: The DOM is a tree of elements.

teaching.text: Every element can hold children, so the page has levels rather than one flat row.

prompt.text: The <html> element wraps the <head> and the

answer.text: The <html> element wraps the <head> and the body.

hints: It holds what is actually shown on the page.
cards.fullLine: The <html> element wraps the <head> and the body.

prompt.text: Title, meta tags and stylesheet links live in the

answer.text: Title, meta tags and stylesheet links live in the head.

hints: It is the part a reader never sees drawn.
cards.fullLine: Title, meta tags and stylesheet links live in the head.

teaching.text: Metadata and stylesheet links describe the page but are never painted.

prompt.text: Which method returns the first element that matches a CSS selector?

hints: The plural version returns a list instead.
cards.fullLine: querySelector returns the first element that matches a CSS selector.

teaching.text: The plural form returns every match as a list, even when only one exists.

prompt.text: Changing an element's classList does what?

hints: The DOM in memory is what the browser draws.
cards.fullLine: Changing an element's classList updates the live page.

prompt.text: The words inside a paragraph form a

answer.text: The words inside a paragraph form a text node.

hints: It cannot hold children of its own.
cards.fullLine: The words inside a paragraph form a text node.

prompt.text: Which property reads or replaces all the words inside an element?

hints: The other common property parses its string as markup.
cards.fullLine: textContent reads or replaces all the words inside an element.

teaching.text: innerHTML parses its string as markup; this property treats it as plain characters.

prompt.text: Which is safer when showing text written by a learner?

hints: One of these would let a tag become real markup.
cards.fullLine: textContent is safer when showing text written by a learner.

prompt.text: Every element, text and comment in the DOM is a

answer.text: Every element, text and comment in the DOM is a node.

hints: Different kinds share the same tree vocabulary.
cards.fullLine: Every element, text and comment in the DOM is a node.

teaching.text: Elements, words and comments all sit in one tree as separate points.

teaching.alt: A page drawn as a tree: html branching into head and body, body branching into a heading, a paragraph and a list

teaching.search: The JavaScript DOM explained in 5 minutes
teaching.alt: A short tour of the DOM as a tree of nodes

cards.summary: View Source is not the live DOM

prompt.text: Why can the Elements panel show HTML that View Source does not?

hints: One view is the sent bytes; the other is what runs now.
cards.fullLine: The Elements panel differs from View Source because script changed the live DOM.

teaching.text: View Source shows the bytes the server sent; the Elements panel shows what runs now.
